slides.hook: Migrant roofers who rebuild storm-damaged homes drink more when the work is riskier, their housing is crowded, and family is far away. Many say beer dulls the fear and the monotony of the job.
slides.title: Beer and the labor process: how risk-taking, crowded housing, and family separation shape drinking behaviors among migrant roofers
Bad timing: mass-participatory asset bubbles as a mechanism of predatory inclusion
slides.snippet: This paper considers the relationship between market composition and temporal dynamics of ethno-racial stratification in mass-participatory asset bubbles. Beginning from the insight that bubbles possess the social structure of a Ponzi scheme, we first ask to what extent timing of entry is structured by racial status and associated resource disparities among participants.

slides.book_title: Gray Is Beautiful: Confronting the Retreat of Democracy from the Radical Center

slides.title: Roles in Sociological Field Observations

slides.hook: Immigrants' views on abortion shift toward those of their new country over time and across generations, even when they move somewhere more conservative than where they came from.
slides.title: Between beliefs and borders: migration, religion, and abortion attitudes
slides.authors: Alessandro Ferrara, Yasemin Nuhoğlu Soysal, and Alicia Vignali

slides.title: The code of cohesion: adolescent network centrality, offending, and the downside of school cohesion
slides.snippet: Paradoxical to numerous theories and policies, adolescents attending schools high in student cohesion do not reliably exhibit less involvement in offending. Coleman’s arguments about status and norms and the broader literature on adolescent networks suggest that this paradox is partially attributable to high-status males having more leeway to offend when attending schools high in student cohesion, which over time reinforces their engagement in offending.

slides.title: Conceptualizing Political Opportunity
slides.authors: D. S. Meyer and D. C. Minkoff

slides.hook: Women in Brazil who had lived through the Zika epidemic drew on that memory to decide whether to have children during the COVID pandemic.
slides.title: Childbearing attitudes amid successive novel infectious disease epidemics: a mixed-method experimental approach
slides.authors: Letícia J Marteleto, Molly Dondero, and Alexandre Gori Maia

slides.title: Organizational status and online-offline mobilization cycles
slides.snippet: Scholars of social movements and culture are increasingly interested in the dynamic relationship between online discourse and offline mobilization. Although prior work typically frames online discourse as a precursor to offline activism, emerging research on right-wing extremist (RWE) mobilization hints at a reciprocal relationship.

slides.book_title: Traders, Speculators, and Captains of Industry: How Capitalist Legitimacy Shaped Foreign Investment Policy in India

slides.title: Housework: Who Did, Does or Will Do It, and How Much Does It Matter?
slides.authors: S. M. Bianchi, L. C. Sayer, M. A. Milkie, and J. P. Robinson

slides.hook: When young women's beliefs about premarital sex clash with what they actually want, their behavior follows the desire, not the belief.
slides.title: Discordant attitudes, desires, and behaviors: sexual cognitive dissonance in the transition to adulthood
slides.authors: Michelle A Eilers and Abigail Weitzman

slides.title: What we talk about when we talk about guns: four decades of firearms coverage in the New York Times
slides.authors: Brett C Burkhardt and Aimee Dinnín Huff
slides.snippet: Guns are potent cultural objects in the United States, a fact that has spurred much recent social science research. Much of that work examines the beliefs, discourses, and actions of gun enthusiasts.

slides.book_title: Shadows of the Enlightenment: The Hidden Politics and Ideology of the Natural and Social Sciences

slides.title: Anti-Immigrant Prejudice in Europe: Contact, Threat Perception, and Preferences for the Exclusion of Migrants

slides.hook: To build affordable housing in well-off suburbs, developers often skip the fight. Rather than win over likely opponents, a study finds, they quietly work around them.
slides.title: From persuasion to evasion: anti -collective action and the making of affordable housing in suburban Chicago
slides.authors: John N Robinson and Lillian Leung

slides.title: Do occupations confer equal prestige on female and male incumbents?
slides.authors: Maik Hamjediers, Ferdinand Geissler, Johannes Giesecke, and Markus Schrenker
slides.snippet: While common measures of occupational prestige target shared beliefs about occupations at the aggregate level, little is known about whether these apply equally across potentially different incumbents of the same occupation. We address this gap by asking whether occupations confer the same prestige to female and male incumbents.

slides.book_title: Reimagining Aid: Foreign Donors, Women’s Health, and New Paths for Development in Cambodia

slides.title: Feminist Attitudes and Support for Gender Equality: Opinion Change in Women and Men, 1974-1998
slides.authors: C. I. Bolzendahl and D. J. Myers

slides.hook: What it means to be childless depends on where you live. Japanese women described it as increasingly normal, while American women described isolation and moral judgment.
slides.title: Narrations of non-motherhood: how context shapes what it means to be childless in the United States and Japan
Precarious work schedules and flexibility: implications for work-caregiving conflict and parenting stress
slides.authors: Jaeseung Kim and Julia R Henly
slides.snippet: Although there is growing recognition that unstable and unpredictable work schedules create challenges for working parents, research is scarce on whether access to flexibility from different resources can attenuate problems created by scheduling instability. Guided by Emlen’s conceptualization of flexibility and the Job Demands-Resource Model, we examine the buffering effects of flexibility resources—from work, child care, and family—on work-caregiving conflict and parental stress in the context of work schedule instability.

slides.book_title: Who Cares About Parents?: Temporary Alliances, Exclusionary Practices, and the Strategic Possibilities of Parenting Groups

slides.title: Narrations of non-motherhood: how context shapes what it means to be childless in the United States and Japan
slides.snippet: In our era of low fertility rates, much research has examined factors behind delayed childbearing and childlessness. While scholars emphasize the role of macro-level context in constraining reproductive decision-making, less attention has been paid to how context shapes what it means, subjectively, to remain childless today.

slides.hook: Online talk is usually treated as the precursor to street activism. In the White Lives Matter movement, a study finds the two feed each other, cycling back and forth.
slides.title: Organizational status and online-offline mobilization cycles
Conservative politics is more strongly associated with skepticism about science than is conservative religion - and both restrain enthusiasm more than they encourage negativity
slides.snippet: Research on Americans’ attitudes toward science shows that both theologically conservative religious views and political conservatism are associated with negative views of science and scientists. In their efforts to understand the relationship between conservatism and science attitudes, however, authors have often prioritized one type of conservatism—either religious or political—rather than exploring the unique role of each.

slides.book_title: Inside Data Science: Hackers and the Making of a New Profession

slides.title: The global rise in children’s attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder prevalence: a macro-sociological explanation
slides.authors: Irem Tuncer-Ebetürk, Jessica Kim, and Yasemin Nuhoğlu Soysal
slides.snippet: In the past three decades, the global diagnosis rate of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has grown drastically. While existing sociological studies demonstrate the complexity of ADHD diagnoses and treatment in specific national contexts, their ability to explain ADHD’s global growth is limited.

slides.hook: Tight-knit schools are supposed to curb misbehavior. Instead they give high-status boys more leeway, and over time their popularity predicts more offending, not less.
slides.title: The code of cohesion: adolescent network centrality, offending, and the downside of school cohesion
Qualified lotteries can neutralize conflicts of interest in the appointment of individuals to positions of power
slides.snippet: The preferential treatment of relatives, friends, and peers is, and has always been, a problem in the appointment of individuals to positions of power, such as executive managerial positions, judgeships, professorships, or leadership roles in public administration and regulatory agencies. Are there viable institutional alternatives to today’s reliance on recusals and consensus-based selection?

slides.book_title: The Police, Activists, and Knowledge: The Struggle Against Racialized Policing in France

slides.title: Colonial legacy and contemporary civil violence: a global study from 1960 to 2018
slides.snippet: This study assesses whether the legacy of colonialism continues to influence patterns of civil violence in the contemporary era. A large and established quantitative literature attributes civil violence to low levels of economic development and limited political rights, but few quantitative studies consider whether colonial legacy plays an enduring role in such conflicts.

slides.hook: As the 2000s housing bubble peaked, Black and Hispanic buyers bought later than White buyers. Segregation and word of mouth pushed them to buy high, right before the crash.
slides.title: Bad timing: mass-participatory asset bubbles as a mechanism of predatory inclusion
Breaking the mold: the changing modularity of protest forms during cycles of contention
slides.snippet: One crucial decision that every group of protesters needs to make concerns the forms of action through which they want to convey their claims. While repertoires of contention can vary greatly across different sociopolitical contexts, we know little about why some protest forms may acquire or lose prominence within the same polity over relatively short periods.

slides.hook: New Deal mortgage maps downgraded neighborhoods based on where appraisers imagined Black residents, not where they actually lived. Racial assumptions drove the risk scores.
slides.title: The spatial logic of racial devaluation in the Home Owners’ Loan Corporation
Is it good to work with? Workability and the meaning of non-native species in urban policy
slides.authors: Tyler J Bateman, Daniel Silver, Alicia Eads, and Charlotte Kafka-Gibbons
slides.snippet: Research on social problems often analyzes how different groups think or act in relation to a single issue. Less frequent are studies of how a single group thinks or acts in relation to many phenomena, any of which may be construed as problematic to a greater or lesser degree.

slides.hook: Income mobility has held steady for men but slipped for women. A study of Swedish data finds the reason: education increasingly ties a woman's income to her parents'.
slides.title: Explaining gender-specific trends in income mobility: the role of education
Examining the relationship between male-breadwinning and divorce: the impact of work-family policies in the United States
slides.snippet: There is ongoing debate as to whether gender specialization, historically considered to be the most efficient family arrangement, or gender egalitarianism, now typically seen as more economically and ideologically desirable, is more negatively associated with divorce in the contemporary United States. In the context of a stalled gender revolution, I draw upon gender equity theory to explore whether differential levels of institutional support for gender equality in the home, operationalized as state-level work-family policy supports, help explain why traditional gender arrangements are still often associated with marital stability among different gender couples.

slides.hook: Tax credits for workers are meant to fight poverty. A cross-national study finds more generous ones can actually track higher in-work poverty, unless they target low earners.
slides.title: Can earned income tax credits earn their keep?: earned income tax credits and in-work poverty in comparative perspective
The role of graduate education in the rising wage premium for professional and managerial occupations, 1980–2019
slides.authors: Felix Busch, Paula England, and Wenhao Jiang
slides.snippet: Part of the rise in US wage inequality comes from a widening gap between professional/managerial (PM) and other occupations (NPM). We examine the role of education in the trend in this gap from 1980 to 2019.

slides.hook: What predicts blaming Asian Americans for COVID? A new study points to Christian nationalism and a moral outlook built on loyalty and authority over care and fairness.
slides.title: Belonging and blame: cultural and moral correlates of anti-Asian scapegoating for the COVID-19 pandemic

slides.hook: Even in secular China, religion shapes cultural taste. Areas dense with Buddhist temples show narrower musical tastes; Taoist temple areas show wider ones.
slides.title: The selectiveness of inclusiveness: exploring the influence of traditional religious visage on contemporary cultural tastes
slides.authors: Wen Ma, Ying Li, and Yunsong Chen
